transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Jon Park (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Patel (CISO, Helix Diagnostics), Luis Rios (Platform Eng), Hannah Cho (Head of IT)

Summary (auto): quick security intake focused on compliance and key management for PII/ePHI. Next steps captured at end.

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm samira from redwood. we've got jon from our se team. can you each do quick intros?
[00:12] Maya: yeah hi, i'm maya patel, ciso at helix, responsible for risk and compliance.
[00:16] Luis: luis, platform engineer, i own infra and onboarding.
[00:19] Hannah: hannah, head of it, we'll be owning the integration side.
[00:23] Jon: great, jon park, i run solutions for dedicated and private deployments, especially around k m s and network isolation - thanks for taking the time.

[00:35] Samira: quick agenda, do a security posture intake, cover SOC2 and ISO status, talk auth (SSO/SAML), RBAC, audit logs, and KMS/encryption. then discuss deployment options - hosted, dedicated, private - and map to your requirements. sound good?
[00:48] Maya: yes, that covers it. high level, helix handles diagnostic records - we treat lots of ePHI, so we need a b a a and long term retention on some logs, possibly 7 years for certain audit artifacts. also want to make sure we can do SSO via our samel provider, and have strict role separation.

[01:10] Jon: noted. on the b a a, redwood does support B A A in private deployments, and we have enterprise contracts for dedicated as well. for hosted we have a variation - we can sign a b a a in some cases but there are network/residency constraints. samira, want to add the specifics?
[01:30] Samira: sure. for hosted API customers, we do offer BAA for healthcare customers but there are additional controls we evaluate - e.g., data residency and log retention SLAs. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and isolated GPU pools; Private (VPC or on-prem) is the strongest for your regulatory demands because you control the network and keys.

[01:55] Maya: can you explain the K M S story? we are required to use our KMS / HSM for key custody, keys must be customer-managed, and we need to prove that private keys never leave our HSM.
[02:08] Jon: yes. we support customer-managed KMS integrations. for cloud we integrate with AWS KMS and CloudHSM, also GCP KMS and external HSMs via PKCS#11 for private deployments. for hosted, we offer envelope encryption where you bring a key via a partner KMS and we encrypt tokens at rest, but for true HSM-backed custody you'd likely want private or dedicated with HSM fronting. sometimes the transcript auto shows "CMS"—sorry that's a transcription quirk.
[02:38] Luis: and key rotation? we need rotation without downtime and full audit trail.
[02:42] Jon: we can support rotation workflows; with envelope keys you can rotate master keys in your KMS and rewrap data keys. we log key operations and issue audit records. the difference: hosted has managed rewraps; private lets you run your own HSM, which gives the most provable custody.

[03:05] Hannah: audit logs — we need immutable logs with retention policies. some of our compliance requires 7 years. what's the retention model?
[03:14] Samira: we ship audit logs to our platform logs and can also forward to customer sinks (S3, GCS, or SIEM). logs are append-only; for dedicated/private we can configure longer retention and store redacted payloads or full request/response depending on your data classification. for hosted we have standard retention windows, but we can negotiate extended retention as an enterprise add-on.

[03:40] Maya: do you support field-level redaction or PII masking before logs leave the service? we can't have full ePHI in third-party logs unless it's covered by the BAA.
[03:49] Jon: yes, we have configurable masking where you can redact specific fields at the ingress or redact prompt blocks. we also offer prefix caching that can be disabled for sensitive workloads. sometimes transcription will say "prefix cache" weirdly but it's just a net optimization.

[04:08] Luis: what about RBAC and least privilege? we need separation of duties between dev, ops, and compliance. can we map roles to our SSO groups?
[04:15] Samira: we support RBAC with role templates and you can map to SAML groups. our console supports scoped API tokens and per-route permissions. Jon, any notes on fine-grained policies?
[04:25] Jon: you can create granular roles, e.g., model deployer, infra operator, auditor. we also have token-level scopes so you can issue keys that can only call embeddings or only call logs retrieval endpoints. that helps if you want to minimize blast radius.

[04:44] Maya: is there support for MFA enforced via our IdP?
[04:48] Samira: yes, we delegate auth to your IdP so MFA policies apply. SAML SSO will enforce whatever policies you have configured. we've seen customers use Okta, Azure AD, and Ping.

[05:02] Hannah: what about auditability of admin actions? we need to know when keys are rotated, users created, or rollbacks happened.
[05:09] Jon: we capture admin events as part of the audit log stream; these are immutable events with user, timestamp, and context. for private deployments, you can also push logs to your SIEM and attach detention policies.

[05:25] Maya: encryption in transit and at rest? any customer data in memory exposure?
[05:30] Jon: TLS for all transit; at rest we encrypt with KMS-wrapped data keys. for in-memory exposures, our runtime minimizes token retention and zeroes memory where possible, but if you need complete control you can run private on-prem where you control the hardware. small caveat—very complex on-prem setups may need extra engineering time.

[05:56] Luis: we will need network restrictions — egress controls, VPC peering, private endpoints. how do you support that?
[06:03] Samira: Dedicated supports private networking and VPC peering into your cloud account. Private deployments run inside your VPC or on-prem. For hosted, we offer IP allowlisting and private endpoints on request, but if you need no public egress then private is the typical choice.

[06:20] Maya: what about SOC2 and ISO? do you have current attestations?
[06:26] Samira: yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certification. i'll send the SOC2 report; note it will be redacted. Jon can attach the certs and our security whitepaper.
[06:37] Jon: i'll add those to the CRM. also we have penetration testing reports we can share under NDA.

[06:44] Hannah: sample audit export format? we want to validate ingest to our SIEM.
[06:48] Jon: logs are JSON lines with standard fields: timestamp, principal, action, resource, request_id. we can provide a sample export and a syslog/forwarder integration doc.

[07:02] Maya: retention and deletion: some of our data must be kept 7 years, some 1 year. can we set different windows per data class?
[07:09] Samira: yes. retention is policy-driven. you can tag data classes and apply retention rules. for Hosted we maintain the policies for you; for Private you control retention placement and lifecycle rules. we'll need a matrix from you to map classes to windows.

[07:25] Luis: performance tradeoffs—if we disable prefix caching and use full redaction, how does latency change?
[07:30] Jon: there is a measurable delta. caching reduces token costs and latency; without it latency might increase by 10-30% depending on prompt mix. we can quantify in the SE deep dive and run a benchmark with your sample prompts.

[07:46] Maya: any customers in healthcare you can reference with similar constraints?
[07:50] Samira: yes, we have a few healthcare customers on dedicated and private deployments; i'll share anonymized references and a case study.

[07:58] Hannah: how do you handle data residency? we have some EU-only data.
[08:03] Jon: region pinning is supported. for hosted we host in multiple regions and you can choose where data is stored. Dedicated/private gives you stronger guarantees. for EU-only workloads we recommend a private or dedicated region where data does not leave the EU.

[08:17] Maya: ok good. what about legal — do you have an established procurement flow for BAA + SOC2 customers? we need a draft contract to start the legal review.
[08:24] Samira: yes. we have a standard BAA addendum and procurement templates. i'll share the contract request and redwood's standard terms. legal reviews normally take a couple of weeks depending on redlines.

[08:39] Luis: small nit — for hosted, you mentioned log redaction. is that done client-side or server-side?
[08:44] Jon: both options. we support client-side redaction libraries you can run before sending; server-side redaction is configurable on ingress. many customers prefer client-side for maximum separation.

[08:58] Maya: any certifications for cryptographic modules or HSM?
[09:02] Jon: when using CloudHSM, the cloud provider certs apply; for external HSMs we support FIPS-140-2/3 compliant modules depending on the vendor. we'll provide specifics in the follow-up doc.

[09:16] Samira: quick recap and proposed plan: we'll send SOC2 and security whitepaper, provide sample audit logs and retention doc, and schedule a deep dive with jon to size Dedicated/Private and run a benchmark. helix will provide retention matrix and BAA scope. sound right?

[09:32] Maya: yes. can we aim to have the SOC2 and the sample logs this week?
[09:36] Samira: yes, i'll send by friday 11/06. jon, can you be available for the deep dive week of 11/09?
[09:42] Jon: yep, i'll block time.

[09:46] Hannah: last question — pricing and SLAs for Dedicated vs Private, ballpark?
[09:51] Samira: high level: Dedicated is monthly reserved capacity with SLA; Private involves licensing/support and on-prem costs. i'll include ballpark numbers in the follow-up but we'll need usage estimates to finalize.

[10:05] Maya: thank you, that was useful.
[10:08] Samira: thank you all, we'll follow up with docs and next steps.
[10:12] Meeting ended.
